text:
maria: heads up — we have a p99 spike on /v1/chat in us-west-2 since ~03:12 UTC. Affects gpt-redwood-13b (seq=1024/2048 paths). p95 ~2x, p99 ~3-4x over baseline. Canary showed it started right after last nightly compile/pack.

oncall-bot: alert: high_p99_latency /v1/chat (us-west-2) — triggered 03:13 UTC — incident id: #INC-8391 :rotating_light:

sandeep: thanks — do we know what changed in the compile? any new attention flags?

maria: nightly build enabled ENABLE_FUSED_SDPA=yes and set NVCC_FLAGS="-O3 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -ftree-vectorize" for kernel experiment. Also ENABLE_TILE_FUSE=1.

support-alex: several customers (enterprise tier) opened support tickets about slow responses on long messages. ticket ids: T-4421, T-4425. They show server-side token generation stalls.

jess: can you paste kernel selection logs / any perf traces?

maria: paste logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:15Z] kernel_picker: model=gpt-redwood-13b seq_len=2048 batch=1 selected=sdpa_fused_v2 score=0.94
[2026-03-16T03:12:15Z] kernel_runner: launch attention sdpa_fused_v2 grid=(128,1,1) time=9.4ms p95
[2026-03-16T03:12:16Z] kernel_runner: fallback_to_legacy=false
[2026-03-16T03:12:17Z] perf: token_latencies=(0:1.2ms,512:2.9ms,1024:6.2ms,2048:18.3ms)
```

maria: note that before the change we were using legacy_sdpa (non-fused) with consistent ~4.5ms for 2048. The fused path shows much higher variance for long sequences.

sandeep: weird — fused should be faster. Could be divergence under certain head dims or shared memory footprint causing eviction. Any OOMs or L2 thrashing?

maria: no OOMs reported, memory headroom fine. But observed kernel occupancy logs show high shared mem usage and warp divergence counters rising.

ryan: can we force kernel selection back to legacy for the chat route as an immediate mitigation? If we can flip a runtime flag we avoid a full rollback.

maria: trying now. toggling REDWOOD_ATTENTION_MODE=legacy for route /v1/chat in us-west-2. Applying via rollout API...

ops-bot: rollout started: route=/v1/chat region=us-west-2 env.REDWOOD_ATTENTION_MODE=legacy scope=canary(10%)

maria: canary metrics look promising — p95 down to ~1.8x baseline, p99 trending down. Scaling to 100%...

ops-bot: rollout completed: 100% — route=/v1/chat region=us-west-2

sandeep: good. For root cause we need to repro locally. Maria, can you capture a small reproducible harness? maybe run the fused kernel with seq=2048 and instrument L2/shared mem counters.

maria: made a repro script and ran on a dev GPU (A100). Repro steps:
1) checkout nightly branch with ENABLE_FUSED_SDPA=1 and ENABLE_TILE_FUSE=1
2) build with NVCC_FLAGS above
3) run ./perf_harness --model gpt-redwood-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --profile kernels

Logs show a clear jump in attention kernel latency only when ENABLE_TILE_FUSE=1 + ENABLE_FUSED_SDPA=1 combined. If I enable fused SDPA but disable tile fuse, latency is close to baseline.

jess: so interaction between tile fusion + fused sdpa causing regression. That’s an important note. Any compile-time flags that could alter behavior? e.g., -use_fast_math or vectorization heuristics?

maria: NVCC_FLAGS had -ftree-vectorize enabled. I toggled it off in a dev build, perf improved ~15% but still worse than legacy. Biggest delta is tile_fuse interaction.

support-alex: we need a hotfix for customers — the runtime toggle helped, but we should ship a patch to disable tile fusion in nightly until we fully validate. Also update runbook steps so support can flip mode.

sandeep: agreed. Plan: 1) keep REDWOOD_ATTENTION_MODE=legacy for prod chat route (done) 2) mark nightly compile config to disable ENABLE_TILE_FUSE by default 3) add a perf canary test for seq >= 1024 long sequences that runs after compile 4) dig into kernel memory layout and warp divergence with nvprof / nsight.

maria: created PR to update nightly build flags: PR #7921 — sets ENABLE_TILE_FUSE=0 and documents why. Also added a canary job in CI: long-seq-perf (seq=1024/2048) that fails build on >1.15x p99 regression.

ryan: FYI I notified the impacted customers via support notes and mentioned temporary mitigation + ETA for patch.

ops-bot: incident update: mitigation applied (runtime flag), patch PR opened, customers notified. Incident state: mitigated.

jess: follow-ups — assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml for root cause. Add a postmortem if customers were affected SLA-wise. Also add a checklist entry to ensure we run long-seq perf canaries on kernel changes.

sandeep: I'll take kernel investigation. Maria, if you can attach perf traces and nvprof outputs to PR that’ll help.

maria: will upload nvprof traces + the perf_harness results to PR and ticket. Leaving the runtime flag in place until tile fuse is validated.

support-alex: closing customer tickets as mitigated and waiting for final fix.

maria: thanks everyone. summary: compile-time tile fusion + fused sdpa caused p99 regressions for long sequences. Immediate mitigation was runtime fallback to legacy kernels. Patch to nightly config opened and CI canary added. Postmortem to follow. :white_check_mark:
